transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… work, mostly. I’ve been making technical mistakes I really should know better than to make—labeling camera cards wrong, missing timecode notes, that kind of thing. The one that really got to me was exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third, even after I’d checked it. It’s embarrassing, and it kind of scared me into coming in.
Have you been worrying a lot lately?
Um… I don’t know. Not “worrying” exactly, I guess. I mean, I’m concerned about work, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed myself worrying a lot in general.
When you were a child, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying organized?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t remember all of it clearly, but in elementary school teachers would move my desk around because I was always getting up, calling out answers, or distracting other kids before I even noticed I was doing it.
Do you still often have trouble staying focused on what you’re doing?

Yeah… I mean, it shows up that way. I’ll think I’m focused, but then I miss something obvious, like a timecode note, or I label a camera card wrong. The lower-third thing I mentioned… I had checked it, and it still went out wrong. So, yeah, I guess staying locked in on the details is a problem.
Do these kinds of attention mistakes also happen outside of work?

Um… outside work, it’s less obvious, I guess. The things that really scared me were at work — like labeling camera cards wrong, missing a timecode note, or sending out a cut with the wrong lower-third even after I thought I checked it. That’s the stuff I know better than to mess up.
Did these concentration mistakes get noticeably worse after something stressful happened in your life?

Kind of, yeah. It got more noticeable after the company readjustment changed how my shoots and edit reviews run. That was… about two years ago. A little over two years, maybe two years and a couple months. Since then it’s been disruptive like this.
Do these attention problems also cause problems at home?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it causing the same kind of problems at home… or at least nothing that stands out the way work does.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory?
Not really… I mean, I forget little things sometimes, but I haven’t noticed any major memory problem.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
Not really… I mean, I have off days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed.
When you feel stressed, do your mistakes and concentration problems get noticeably worse?

Yeah… I think so. When I’m stressed, I start making these stupid technical mistakes I really should catch—like labeling camera cards wrong, missing a timecode note, or exporting a cut with the wrong lower-third even after I thought I checked it. That’s kind of what pushed me to come in.
Outside of work, do you often feel anxious or on edge?
Not really. I mean… I get tense sometimes, like anyone, but I don’t think I’m generally anxious or on edge outside of work.
Before the work changes happened, did problems with attention or organization ever cause real trouble for you in school, at home, or in relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I guess it did, even back in elementary school. Teachers would move my desk because I was always getting up, blurting things out, or bothering other kids before I really realized I was doing it.
Growing up, did your attention or impulsive behavior cause problems anywhere besides school?
I’m not really sure. School is the main place I remember it being a problem. Outside of that… I don’t have a clear example, honestly.
Have attention or organization problems caused trouble for you in your personal life as an adult?
I don’t know… not in a way I can clearly point to. I mean, things get messy or I put stuff off sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d say it’s caused real trouble personally.
As an adult, have these attention or organization problems caused clear problems in any setting outside of work?
Not really that I can think of. I mean, outside of work I don’t… I don’t have a clear example where it caused a real problem.
Have you had a head injury?
Not that I can think of. I mean, nothing serious comes to mind.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a neurological illness?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been told I have anything like that.
Since the work changes happened, have you often felt anxious about work?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve been stressed at times, but I don’t know that I’d call it often anxious, exactly.
Have you started having trouble managing everyday tasks, like paying bills or keeping appointments?
I don’t think so. I mean, nothing that really stands out… I still get the usual stuff done, as far as I can tell.
In your personal life, do attention or organization problems ever cause real trouble?
Not that I can really point to. I mean, I’m sure I’m not perfectly organized, but I don’t think it’s caused any major trouble personally.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports concentration problems and increased technical mistakes that became noticeably worse after a workplace readjustment about a little over 2 years ago, with stress clearly exacerbating symptoms. There is functional impairment primarily at work. Full ADHD criteria are not established because current impairment is not confirmed across multiple settings, despite childhood symptoms suggestive of ADHD. Mild neurocognitive disorder is less likely given no major memory complaints, preserved everyday task management, and no neurological illness or head injury reported. The presentation is most consistent among the listed options with adjustment disorder with mixed disturbance of emotions and conduct/other symptoms, centered on a psychosocial work stressor.
